answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying each identity to one locked stake and a unique signing cipher: before voting, an agent posts a bond that is slashed if it is ever caught casting two votes. Every fake identity must post its own bond, so an attacker seeking N sybils pays N times the stake and the cost scales linearly with the whole nebula of clones. Honest agents instead accumulate a reef of reputation that a fresh impostor cannot cheaply counterfeit.
